judgment.thesis: Jelmyto was the first FDA-approved drug for low-grade UTUC and Zusduri extends the proprietary RTGel platform into intermediate-risk bladder cancer, a regulatory and formulation moat. Q3 revenue tripled to $89.0M with the first operating profit ($8.3M), but the balance sheet is stretched and receivables jumped.
judgment.breaks_if: Quarterly revenue stalls or receivables keep outgrowing sales (channel stocking), or a competing intravesical therapy wins share.
judgment.customers: Urologists/hospitals via specialty distributors; concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Accounts receivable up $84M to $117M in nine months
Shareholders' deficit of $125M; $189M debt plus $125M prepaid forward obligation
Two products on one generic drug (mitomycin)

judgment.thesis: A roll-up of acquired rare-disease products, several of them generics, now profitable with Q3 product sales of $57.9M vs $22.5M. Growth is bought through licenses (INCRELEX, GALZIN, IMPAVIDO, LIBERVANT, ASN-001) rather than proven organic demand.
judgment.breaks_if: Organic sales of existing products stall, or generic competition hits carglumic acid, betaine or nitisinone.
judgment.customers: Patients via specialty pharmacies; payer/pharmacy concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Q3 net income boosted by $12.9M tax valuation-allowance release
Three products are generics with little protection
Accrued Medicaid rebates and specialty-pharmacy dependence

judgment.thesis: Revenue is up 72% in the latest quarter and the company just turned operating-profitable (Q3 operating income of $30M versus a $41M loss a year ago), with data center optical DSP exposure and a jump in prepaid assets. But this looks like a cyclical rebound from a trough in a competitive fabless chip business, and the evidence for durable switching costs or named wins is missing.
judgment.breaks_if: Gross margin stalls near 58% and the quarterly revenue run-rate of about $218M fades, with inventory and receivables still growing faster than sales, which would indicate a restocking bounce rather than durable demand.
judgment.customers: Distributors, module makers, OEMs and ODMs; data center end customers (Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Google) are named only as end markets, and customer concentration is not quantified in the supplied text.
red_flags: Recovery from a deep trough (revenue previously declined, 9-month operating loss a year ago of $112M), so this is not a clean inflection
No backlog, named design wins or contract figures supplied; the business section lists end markets and customers only generically
Inventory up 46% and receivables up 59% since December, which could signal channel stuffing or a restocking cycle; prepaid and other current assets also rose 14
Nine-month net loss of $14M after a $17M tax charge; debt rose to $164M with another credit amendment; share count up 4%
Terminated Silicon Motion merger, with arbitration and class action and potential damages; auditor change in June 2026

judgment.thesis: A semiconductor assembly-equipment leader riding a sharp cyclical upturn: Q3 revenue $330M vs $148M and deferred revenue +214%. Equipment orders are cyclical and the prior year's loss came from impairments and an exited business, so this looks more like a cycle than a structural inflection.
judgment.breaks_if: Orders and deferred revenue roll over as customers digest capacity.
judgment.customers: IDMs, OSATs and foundries; concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Prior-year results distorted by EA business exit and impairment
Manufacturing in Israel and China (geopolitical risk)

judgment.thesis: STAAR is the leading phakic ICL maker with proprietary Collamer, a real niche advantage. But Q3 sales fell 12% and gross margin dropped; the nine-month gain is a rebound from the 2025 China destocking collapse, not a new inflection.
judgment.breaks_if: Quarterly sales keep declining or China demand fails to recover.
judgment.customers: Surgeons via direct sales and distributors in 85+ countries; 91% of revenue outside the US
red_flags: Latest quarter revenue -12% with gross margin falling
Recovery from a collapse, not inflection
Failed Alcon merger and governance changes

judgment.thesis: A cable/streaming news broadcaster whose Q3 profit rests on a one-off $14M termination fee; excluding it, operating income was near zero. Carriage and brand give some position, but nothing points to structural demand growth.
judgment.breaks_if: Service revenue growth slows without one-off fees, or settlement payments strain cash.
judgment.customers: Advertisers, MVPD carriage partners and subscribers; concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Q3 included a $14M one-off termination fee

judgment.thesis: Motiva implants hold US PMA approval in a market with only three other US-approved makers and show strong safety data. Revenue grows 34% with losses narrowing, but it is still loss-making and leveraged.
judgment.breaks_if: US launch adoption stalls or operating losses widen again.
judgment.customers: Plastic surgeons via direct sales and exclusive distributors; concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Still operating at a loss (-7% margin)

judgment.thesis: Wireless IoT chips with long design-in lifecycles give a real edge, and revenue grew 22% to a small Q3 profit. But Texas Instruments has agreed to buy the company for $231 cash, which caps the upside.
judgment.breaks_if: The TI merger closes at $231 (fixed payout) or breaks for regulatory reasons.
judgment.customers: Electronics manufacturers worldwide; concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Pending $231/share cash acquisition by TI caps upside

judgment.thesis: Workiva is embedded in SEC and financial reporting at over 85% of the Fortune 1000, giving high switching costs. Backlog +17%, deferred revenue +15% and subscription revenue +17% show steady compounding demand.
judgment.breaks_if: Remaining performance obligations growth drops below 10% or net retention falls.
judgment.customers: 6,600+ organizations incl. 85% of the Fortune 1000; no concentration
red_flags: Sustainability/CSRD demand subject to regulatory rollback
Sales and marketing still 43% of revenue

judgment.thesis: A mid-market ITSM/CX software vendor with backlog +19% and deferred revenue +16%, now modestly profitable. It faces larger rivals and growth is slowly decelerating.
judgment.breaks_if: Backlog growth falls toward revenue growth or SMB churn rises.
judgment.customers: 75,000 businesses; over 60% of ARR from 250+ employee customers
red_flags: Intense competition in ITSM and CX
Profit helped by cost cuts rather than demand

judgment.thesis: Energy drink brands with PepsiCo as primary distributor; recent growth comes mostly from buying Alani Nu and Rockstar. Organic demand evidence is thin and promotional allowances are swelling.
judgment.breaks_if: Same-brand sales decline or promotional spend keeps rising faster than revenue.
judgment.customers: PepsiCo is the primary US/Canada distributor ($390M of $667M receivables)
red_flags: Accrued promotional allowance up from $308M to $479M
Consumer brand with no structural moat

judgment.thesis: A refiner whose Q3 profit swing came from crack spreads, not anything durable. Margins follow commodity prices.
judgment.breaks_if: Crack spreads normalize.
judgment.customers: Wholesale fuel buyers and jobbers; concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Commodity business with no pricing power

judgment.thesis: Marqeta's card issuing platform has integration switching costs, but revenue growth slowed to 8% and backlog fell 18%. Q3 net income was mostly a $104M tax benefit.
judgment.breaks_if: Backlog keeps shrinking or a major customer renegotiates.
judgment.customers: Fintechs and card program operators; concentration not disclosed here
red_flags: Q3 net income mostly from $104M tax benefit

judgment.thesis: Klaviyo's B2C CRM serves 193,000+ businesses and shows building demand: backlog +63%, deferred revenue +43%, revenue +25%. The moat is moderate given Shopify dependence and competition.
judgment.breaks_if: Backlog growth falls back toward revenue growth or the Shopify relationship weakens.
judgment.customers: 193,000+ businesses, mainly e-commerce; reliant on Shopify integration

judgment.thesis: This is not a diamond. PBF is a merchant refiner whose margin swing from -2% to +10% looks like a cyclical and commodity-price recovery, helped by a rebound from the 2025 Martinez fire outage, and its fuels have no switching costs. The material agreements are debt financings (a revolver, 7.25% senior notes and 0% exchangeable notes), not customer wins, and they signal a capital-hungry business that is diluting shareholders.
judgment.breaks_if: The thesis that this is a cyclical, price-driven recovery would be wrong only if margins held at current levels after crack spreads normalize and Martinez and Chalmette are fully running, which would be evidence of a structural advantage. A fall in refining margins or another outage would confirm it
judgment.customers: not disclosed; sells unbranded fuels and petrochemical feedstocks to the wholesale market across the US, Canada and Mexico. Logistics revenue is mostly intercompany with PBF Holding.
red_flags: Commodity refiner: margins follow crack spreads and crude prices, not pricing power
Revenue growth (+32% over twelve months, +59% in the latest quarter) likely reflects fuel prices and recovery from the Martinez fire shutdown
Operational and regulatory risk: Martinez fire (federal and state investigations, unknown penalties) and a Chalmette fire in May 2026
Heavy new debt issuance in 2026 (a revolver plus 7.25% and exchangeable notes), and share count up 4%
No backlog, R&D or named customer evidence; the +11% deferred revenue figure is not meaningful for a refiner

judgment.thesis: Allegro is the world's leading magnetic sensor IC supplier by share, with auto design-ins and proprietary BCD process. Revenue +29% looks partly cyclical, and no backlog is disclosed.
judgment.breaks_if: Auto and industrial orders roll over.
judgment.customers: 15,000+ customers incl. major automakers and tier-1 suppliers

judgment.thesis: BILL has SMB payment network effects, but growth slowed to 13% and backlog fell 24%. Interest on customer funds makes up 11% of revenue.
judgment.breaks_if: Growth falls below 10% or interest income drops with rates.
judgment.customers: 479,000 SMBs and accounting firms; no concentration
red_flags: Interest float income sensitive to rates

judgment.thesis: SolarEdge is recovering from a collapse in solar demand; gross margin has rebuilt but Q3 revenue fell 4% and losses continue. Competition is intense.
judgment.breaks_if: Revenue keeps falling or gross margin slips.
judgment.customers: Distributors and large installers; concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Recovery from a collapse, not inflection

judgment.thesis: TheRealReal has a real niche position as the largest authenticated luxury resale marketplace, with network effects, over 80% of GMV from repeat consignors, and steady growth of about 19%. It is probably not a diamond: operating income is only just breakeven, the balance sheet is heavily indebted with a stockholders' deficit, and its net profit is flattered by non-cash warrant gains.
judgment.breaks_if: Revenue growth falls below the low teens, or operating margin slips back to negative, while debt service on the roughly $380M of convertible and term notes (including the new $150M Fortress loan) keeps absorbing cash.
judgment.customers: Consumer consignors and buyers: over 1 million active buyers, and over 80% of GMV from repeat consignors. No concentration, but supply depends on luxury-brand goods that the company does not control.
red_flags: Operating income is only $1.5M in Q3 2026 and -$3.1M for nine months; breakeven is not yet profit
Net income is boosted by a $50M non-cash warrant fair-value gain; the accumulated deficit is $1.27B
Stockholders' deficit of $354M, about $380M of notes, and a new $150M Fortress secured term loan in Oct 2026
Cash fell to $130M from $151M while shares rose 5%; dilution continues
Competition is broad and low-barrier (brands, auction houses, other resale platforms); no backlog or contract evidence; news tone negative

judgment.thesis: ServiceTitan is a trades-specific system of record with a 71% gross margin, 21-23% steady growth and operating margin improving from -26% to -13%, so switching costs are plausible. However, the supplied evidence has no named customers, retention or net revenue retention figures, backlog, or signed contracts, and deferred revenue grew only 1%, so this looks like steady SaaS improvement rather than a visible inflection.
judgment.breaks_if: Revenue growth falls below about 18%, or operating margin stops improving while stock-based compensation and share dilution (+5%) continue, or disclosed customer retention and net revenue retention fall.
judgment.customers: Small and mid-sized trades businesses (HVAC, plumbing, roofing, landscaping) plus some PE-owned consolidators; concentration not disclosed in the supplied text.
red_flags: Deferred revenue up only 1% against 21-23% revenue growth, so there is no sign of building prepaid demand
Backlog not reported and no named customers or contracts in the evidence
Still loss-making at -13% operating margin with R&D at 33% of revenue
Share count up 5% in a year, so dilution is eroding shareholder value
Edge claims (largest data asset, only end-to-end platform) are management's own assertions with no retention data

judgment.thesis: Backblaze runs low-cost cloud storage on commodity hardware, a thin edge. A CoreWeave master agreement has driven backlog +768% and Q3 revenue +26%, but demand is concentrated.
judgment.breaks_if: CoreWeave ramp stalls or capacity costs outrun revenue.
judgment.customers: 500,000+ customers, with a large new CoreWeave contract concentrating revenue

judgment.thesis: Decipher Prostate is the only gene expression test in the NCCN prostate risk table with broad Medicare and commercial coverage, a durable diagnostic moat. But demand is steady (+15%) and it was already profitable a year ago.
judgment.breaks_if: Reimbursement cuts or testing volume growth falls below 10%.
judgment.customers: Clinicians/patients; reimbursed by Medicare and commercial payers
red_flags: Q3 operating income fell from $22.9M to $16.6M
Net income boosted by tax benefit

judgment.thesis: MACI is an FDA-approved autologous cartilage implant with few real alternatives, backed by the Epicel burn franchise. Revenue +26% and Q3 operating income of $12.2M show durable growth.
judgment.breaks_if: MACI growth slows or a competing cartilage repair product wins approval.
judgment.customers: Orthopedic surgeons and burn centers; concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Federal award match by name is uncertain

judgment.thesis: Ambarella has proprietary CVflow AI silicon and is moving into automotive and robotics, with backlog up 133% and revenue up 20% while operating losses narrow. But it is still loss-making (-15% operating margin) with R&D at 55% of revenue, no named customers or contracts in the evidence, and design-win cycles that favour larger rivals such as Nvidia, Qualcomm, Mobileye and Hisilicon, so this looks like an ordinary fabless chip company rather than a clear diamond.
judgment.breaks_if: Revenue growth falls below about 10% or gross margin drops below 55% while operating margin stays negative, which would show the backlog is not turning into profitable automotive or edge-AI volume.
judgment.customers: not disclosed; end markets are security cameras, automotive, robotics, drones and consumer cameras. Sales run through distributors such as WT Microelectronics, and the concentration level is not given.
red_flags: Still unprofitable at -15% operating margin; R&D is 55% of revenue
Backlog +133% but deferred/prepaid revenue only +7%, and the backlog's composition and timing are unknown
No named customers, design wins or signed agreements in the supplied text
Growth slowed from +20% to +13% in the latest quarter
Sales through a distributor; share count up 3%; strong competition in edge AI and automotive silicon

judgment.thesis: A direct-to-consumer scrubs brand growing 26% with healthy gross margins, but apparel has low switching costs. It was already profitable a year ago, so this is not really an inflection.
judgment.breaks_if: Active customer growth stalls or tariffs squeeze gross margin.
judgment.customers: 2.9M healthcare professional customers plus TEAMS B2B
red_flags: CBP withhold release order on Jordanian manufacturer

judgment.thesis: Calix's broadband platform for service providers builds stickiness, with backlog +12% and deferred revenue +14%. But Q3 growth slowed to 14%, gross margin fell and inventory rose sharply.
judgment.breaks_if: Inventory keeps building while growth slows.
judgment.customers: Broadband service providers (co-ops, municipalities, ISPs); concentration not disclosed
red_flags: Q3 operating income below last year
